[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلىثلاثةأحرفلازيادةفيه)#780/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Weak triliteral nouns whose pattern matches a verb generally undergo the same weakening as that verb; nouns often preserve the original form, though weakening is more common.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلىثلاثةأحرفلازيادةفيه)#780/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some nouns preserve the underlying form, including القود and الخونة, just as a few augmented verbs do; the usual outcome remains sukūn and weakening.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلىثلاثةأحرفلازيادةفيه)#780/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil analyzes خاف, مال, and راح on the فعِل pattern, comparing them to adjectives like فرق and نزق; forms such as روع and حول also preserve the original pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلىثلاثةأحرفلازيادةفيه)#780/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The فُعُل pattern is not used in its underlying form for these weak roots, because ḍamma on wāw is disliked and would lead to vowel adjustment or hamza, as with أدؤر and خون.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلىثلاثةأحرفلازيادةفيه)#780/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Patterns that are not themselves weak retain their original form; examples include نوم and سولة, while حول, صير, بيع, and ديم follow their stated patterns.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلىثلاثةأحرفلازيادةفيه)#780/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In فُعُل forms with wāw, the wāw is made vowelless to avoid two adjacent ḍammas and the heaviness of wāw; this is preferred to hamza and parallels vowelless nonweak forms such as رسل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلىثلاثةأحرفلازيادةفيه)#780/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poetry may restore a heavy or lengthened form that ordinary speech avoids; Sībawayh quotes ʿAdī ibn Zayd’s line with سور as an example.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلىثلاثةأحرفلازيادةفيه)#780/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The corresponding pattern with yāʾ is treated like a sound form because yāʾ followed by wāw is lighter; غيور and غير illustrate this, with analogous lightening in بيض.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Indefinite and definite nouns on the مفاعل and مفاعيل patterns do not decline because these are plural patterns, less basic than the singular; the verse’s مساجد exemplifies the form.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | شراحيل declines in the diminutive because it is Arabic and used only as a plural.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أجمال and فلوس decline because they are close to singular patterns and can form further broken plurals, as in أقوال/أقاويل and أعراب/أعاريب; resemblance to a singular explains the case treatment.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | مفاعل and مفاعيل are terminal plural patterns and cannot be broken into a further pattern; unlike them, فعول can yield فعائل, as in جدود/جدائد and ركوب/ركائب.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أفعال can be singular for some Arabs; Sībawayh cites الأنعام and the Qur’anic wording نسقيكم مما في بطونه, plus ثوب أكياش and سدوس for the form’s uses. | mentions 16:66
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The yāʾ in بخاتي belongs to the plural formation, unlike the suffixal yāʾ in مدائني; it is part of the pattern just as the dāl is part of مساجد.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports a poetic use of ثماني without nunation; diminutives such as بخاتي and صحار decline after the plural pattern is changed, while ثمان as a singular proper name does not.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ثَمَان is indeclinable as a singular name, whereas صحار is a declinable plural; the yāʾ of ثمان resembles the suffix in قمري, يماني, and شآم.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | رباع and حواري pattern with related forms such as سداسي; عواري, عوادي, and حوالي are broken plurals of حولي, عادي, and عارية, not forms with a newly attached yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | مقاتل and عذافر decline because their pattern can also be singular, unlike the exclusively plural مفاعل and مفاعيل forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The yāʾ of ثماني and رباع is an added nisba-like suffix on فعال, so these forms decline; Sībawayh compares it to يماني and شآم.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | صياقلة declines because its tāʾ is appended after the مفاعل pattern is complete, as with feminine singulars; the suffix transforms the word from its plural pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a suffix creates a form like a singular or compound name, the resulting word declines; مدائني and مساجدي have moved out of the original plural pattern through the added yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some speakers shorten جنادل and ذلاذل to جندل and ذلذل and add nunation as compensation for the deleted alif.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Proper names based on plural patterns decline when diminutivized because the diminutive changes the form; حضاجر is itself a collective plural used as a name for the hyena.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حضاجر names the hyena because the plural evokes its broad belly; Sībawayh cites the Arabic expression أوطب حضاجر as evidence for its collective use.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل)#536/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | سراويل is one Arabicized foreign garment name, but resembles indeclinable forms; as a man’s name it remains indeclinable when diminutivized, like عناق.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفعالالمعتلةمنبناتالثلاثة)#776/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In augmented triliteral verbs, when the consonant before a weak letter was originally vowelless and is not alif, wāw, or yāʾ, the weak letter is made vowelless and its vowel shifts back.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفعالالمعتلةمنبناتالثلاثة)#776/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | This shift lets the added form undergo the same weakening as its unaugmented counterpart, while avoiding a change to a form absent from Arabic; the preceding consonant has already changed.

[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفعالالمعتلةمنبناتالثلاثة)#776/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some verbs preserve the original weak letter despite the preceding sukūn, by analogy with fāʿala; this preservation is exceptional rather than a general rule.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفعالالمعتلةمنبناتالثلاثة)#776/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil explains that اجتوروا and similar forms retain wāw because they mean the equivalent tafāʿala forms, where wāw remains; shared meaning with sound triliteral forms also supports retention.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفعالالمعتلةمنبناتالثلاثة)#776/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A form such as اجتاروا would follow regular weakening if built directly from the triliteral root; اجتوروا is possible when construed on the meaning and pattern of تفاعلوا.
